resolution: Answered the user's marvel at the 40MB file size for the 508 km2 / 776k-instance city (informational, no code). Broke down WHY it is cheap: 54.2 bytes per building (one position+rotation+scale+color instance row, no mesh/verts/texture — all 776k expand from ONE interned cube), ~81 KB per km2, so the entire city is ~1.3 uncompressed 4K screenshots and ~16,000x more disk-efficient per km2 than a GTA V install (caveat: boxes vs art — the real-game gigabytes are art/audio, not world structure; textures+LOD are the next cost, not scale). Confirmed the pasted loader log is healthy (776,084 instances, 2528 frames, clean exit) and flagged its one notable line: 'physics collider cap clipped 771988 rendered instance rows' — only 4096 of 776k objects get colliders (floors-first so the base slab catches the player everywhere, but distant buildings are walk-through). That is the collision frontier; spatial-windowed collision is the offered final piece. Session stands at 7 files / 4 engine wins, still uncommitted pending the user's go-ahead to commit + build spatial collision.
